title: Screen payments without paying twice for a score

blocks.text: The payment gateway hands every incoming payment to `PaymentScreen` before it is booked. Risk has agreed these rules with finance (amounts in cents):

rows: a `Card` whose fraud score is below 60
a `Card` whose fraud score is 60 or more
a `Card` whose fraud score is 90 or more

blocks.text: Where two rows match a payment, the stricter one, lower in the table, wins.

The fraud score comes from the card network through `RiskScores`, and the network bills every call. Last month's invoice was twice what finance expected for the number of card payments, and nobody wants to repeat that.

Write `screen(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/PaymentScreen.java`. Decisions follow the table, a card payment costs at most one score call, and any other payment costs none. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: transfers up to the hold limit, vouchers and card payments get the decision the table gives them
a transfer above 50,000.00 is held, not sent to review, although it is also above the review limit
each card payment costs exactly one score call, whatever its score, and other payments cost none

origin.section: A Guard Runs Only After Its Pattern Matches, and Again for Every Case That Tries It

concepts: A pattern switch tries its cases from the top and runs the first whose pattern matches and whose guard is true; cases are not ranked by how specific they are.
A guard runs only after its pattern matches, and again for every case that tries it, so a call in two guards runs twice; a call made once in the arm doesn't.
The compiler doesn't evaluate guards, so overlapping guarded cases compile silently and their order decides which one wins.
